FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Despite increasing their winning streak to double digits during the week, Real Madrid cannot afford complacency as they continue pursuing La Liga’s summit against an Alavés side back in the win column.

Match News and Current Form

Real Madrid are flourishing on all fronts after extending their perfect record in Europe this season with an emphatic 5-1 win over PSV, a result preceded by a 2-1 La Liga victory over Celta Vigo. Both of those triumphs came at home and extended their winning streak across all competitions to ten matches, inching José Mourinho closer to a historic achievement as he prepares for his first La Liga encounter with Alavés. Not only would a win for the hosts make Alavés the 26th club Mourinho has defeated in this competition, but Real Madrid would also open a league season with seven consecutive home wins for the first time since 2010/11, which was the beginning of his first stint in charge of Los Blancos.

Alavés dug deep to claim a 3-1 win over Deportivo A Coruña in their last outing, ending what was their longest winless run in La Liga since February 2022 (D3, L5). A much better start to the season in the opening month means that Quique Sánchez Flores’ men will start the weekend in ninth place despite their recent struggles, but hitting the road here may put their spot in the top half of the table in jeopardy. Alavés have been far from glorious on their travels lately, winning just one of their last ten away league games (D5, L4) including their most recent trip to the Bernabéu.

Head-to-Head History

Real Madrid have won 18 of their last 20 home matches against Alavés (L2) and each of the last nine overall. Should they win again here, Alavés will register their worst ever run of consecutive defeats against a single opponent in the top-flight.

Win Probability
Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

Real Madrid have scored first in ten of their 11 league wins this term.

Six of Madrid’s last seven competitive home matches saw both teams score.

Six of Alavés’ last seven outings in all competitions saw both teams score.

Just one of Alavés’ last 12 away league games was decided by a 2+ goal margin.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Madrid’s Jude Bellingham should be full of confidence having scored a goal of the season contender in midweek, which was the 12th of his last 16 club goals to come at home. Lucas Boyé had a busy game in the last round, becoming the first Alavés player to score, assist and miss a penalty in a single La Liga game in the 21st century. He could have a late say with three of his last four goals coming after half-time.

Madrid’s Endrick will be a doubt after missing their midweek assignment, as will Alavés’ Hugo Novoa who limped off during their last match.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

For all of Madrid’s recent dominance, they’re still liable to concede, making the Madrid win with both teams scoring market quite eye-catching.

Author: Peter Stavrinou
